text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein warns against settlements in Jerusalem and provoking feelings of anger and violence after Israel decides to go ahead with Jewish construction.
- Parliament rejects Jewish settlements and calls for Arab summit.
- Crown Prince Hassan will visit Israel only if his trip can serve the cause of peace, official source says.
- Prime Minister Kabariti and PLO's Abu Mazen coordinate positions. Kabariti says any change in Jerusalem is a violation of peace accords.
- Stock Market Director Wahib Shaer says 90 European, U.S. and Asian companies are investing in the Amman bourse; investments worth $85 million to date.
- Fifteen parliamentary deputies call for special session to discuss government's internal policies.
- Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu announces war on peace and opens the battle of Jerusalem.
- Deputy Prime Minister Ensour says within two days there will be no Jordanians left in Israeli jails.
- Information Minister Muasher says decision to end monitoring of foreign and Arab newspapers before they enter the country aims to raise level of freedoms in Jordan.
- Jordanian prisoners in Israel to be released in the next two days, according to official sources.
- Regional forum on the issue of Palestinian refugees to open in Amman from 12-13 March.
- Jordan denounces Israeli plan as illegal; violation of U.N. resolutions and danger to peace process. King's letter to Netanyahu says move will not serve any one, including Israelis.
